**Component:** skills/work-planner/scripts/sync.py

## Overview

Work Planner reads a project's long-lived branches from `config/branches` in the main working tree. A change to that statement reaches the main working tree only when the initiative that made it closes, so for the whole life of that initiative every sync run against the project either reports the set unevaluable or answers with the statement the branch under change replaced. This task gives a run the set the branch under delivery carries, and makes a set it cannot read a reported outcome rather than a silent one.

## Problem

- **The statement lands on a branch nobody reads it from.**
  `config/branches` reaches `i11/e09/workspace` when a task merges, and `workspace` only when the initiative's integration branch merges. `long_lived_names` reads the main working tree, which is checked out on the long-lived branch, so it reads the statement as it stood before the initiative started.
- **Sync drops its reporting rather than its confidence.**
  The epic branch of `sync.py` runs `draft_bases`, `review_references` and `unlinked_reviews` only while `LONG_LIVED` is non-empty. A project whose main working tree states nothing gets no draft line and no reference comparison, and the run reads as clean.
- **A delivering session has to fabricate the set.**
  The session that introduced the statement needed a directory holding nothing but `config/branches` to make Sync Epic report the draft base, because neither the main working tree nor any worktree of it stated the names that work had just added.

## Proposal

- **The reading reaches the branch under delivery.**
  The set a run needs is the one the epic base carries. The reading takes it from the ref the run is working against, falling back to the integration-branch derivation wherever that ref states nothing it can use.
- **An unevaluable set is reported, not skipped.**
  Where the set cannot be read, the epic reporting that depends on it names the checks it did not make, so a run that could not check the draft base and the review references does not read as a run that checked them.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 3 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: the statement lands on a branch nobody reads it from; sync drops its reporting rather than its confidence; a delivering session has to fabricate the set. |
| Plan | Each of the 2 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/work-planner/scripts/sync.py`: the reading reaches the branch under delivery; an unevaluable set is reported, not skipped. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/work-planner/scripts/sync.py`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC12, AC13, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

## References

- **R1.** [Work Planner Scripts](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/workspace/skills/work-planner/scripts) — The reading, the epic checks it gates, and the fixture suite that keeps them.

**Component:** skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py

## Overview

A unit's planning record names its work item twice: once in the README a dispatching session writes, and once in the row link Record Work Item composes. The two names are composed by different parties and can disagree, which leaves the epic row pointing at a file that is not there. This task gives the file one composition and refuses a row link the record cannot satisfy.

## Problem

- **The row's link is composed, not read.**
  `deliver.py --item` writes `<record>/<task id in lower case>.md` from the task id alone. It never looks for the file, so a record whose work item carries another name is linked to a path that does not resolve.
- **The README names the file independently.**
  The record's Artifacts table is written when the record is added, before the work item exists. One delivery found a README whose row expected `work-item.md` while the row link addressed `w05.md`.
- **Nothing measures the disagreement.**
  The link lands in the epic body and the README lands in the engineering branch, and no check reads one against the other.

## Proposal

- **One party names the file.**
  The Work Breakdown Guide names a work item for its task id in lower case. The record's README row carries that name, composed the way the row link is, so the two cannot drift.
- **The link is refused where the file is absent.**
  Record Work Item resolves the path it is about to write against the record folder and refuses a name the folder does not hold, so a mismatch is caught at the row rather than at the reader.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 3 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: the row's link is composed, not read; the README names the file independently; nothing measures the disagreement. |
| Plan | Each of the 2 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py`: one party names the file; the link is refused where the file is absent. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC11, AC12, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

## References

- **R1.** [Work Planner Scripts](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/tree/workspace/skills/work-planner/scripts) — The row link, the record layout it addresses, and the fixture suite that keeps them.

**Component:** skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py

## Overview

The shared skill-file check reports a repeated heading only where something already cites it, so a file can carry several headings of one title unnoticed until the first citation lands on the wrong one. The review criteria carry eleven such headings today. The check should report a repeated heading whether or not anything cites it yet.

## Problem

- **The rule waits for a victim.**
  [`check`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9ed47b0d/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L136-L140) reports a duplicate anchor only when that anchor is in the file's callers, so an ambiguity is measured by whether anyone has fallen into it rather than by whether it is there.
- **Eleven ambiguous headings stand in one file.**
  [`review-criteria.md`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9ed47b0d/skills/work-planner/references/review-criteria.md) titles a heading `Problem` four times and `Work Breakdown`, `Title`, `References`, `Open Questions` and `Non-Goals` twice each, one per issue kind. None is cited, so the check is silent on all of them, and the next author who cites one by title reaches the first of that title.
- **The fault is known to recur.**
  Five citations into that same file resolved by file order until [#1324](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1324) corrected the headings behind them. Those headings were indistinguishable from the eleven that remain.

## Proposal

- **A repeated heading is reported wherever it stands.**
  The check reports a second heading resolving to an anchor another heading in the same file already holds, naming both lines, whether or not a citation reaches it. A link's destination is then unambiguous by construction rather than by nobody having tried it.
- **The remaining repeats are given their kind.**
  Each repeated heading in the review criteria takes the issue kind into its title, as the Proposal and Acceptance Criteria headings already do, so every anchor in the file names one section.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 3 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: the rule waits for a victim; eleven ambiguous headings stand in one file; the fault is known to recur. |
| Plan | Each of the 2 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py`: a repeated heading is reported wherever it stands; the remaining repeats are given their kind. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC13, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

**Component:** skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py

## Overview

A heading written directly beneath a list item, with no blank line between them, renders as list text rather than as a heading in a strict CommonMark reader, and the shared skill-file check does not report it. One such heading stands in the Work Planner review criteria. The check should measure it, so a section cannot silently stop being one.

## Problem

- **A heading can be swallowed by the list above it.**
  [`review-criteria.md`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9ed47b0d/skills/work-planner/references/review-criteria.md#L78-L79) puts `#### Whole` immediately after a bullet's continuation line. A reader that treats the run as one list item never sees the heading, so the section and its anchor are not there for it.
- **The check reads the line as a heading regardless.**
  [`scan`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9ed47b0d/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L54) matches a heading by its leading hashes alone, so a citation to `#whole` resolves for the check while a strict reader finds nothing.
- **Nothing else measures the spacing.**
  The check already measures a trailing blank line, bold-lead width, bullet shape and prose length, so file layout is its concern; this is the one spacing fault it passes over.

## Proposal

- **A heading needs a blank line above it.**
  The check reports a heading whose preceding line is neither blank nor the start of the file, naming the heading. A fenced block's contents stay exempt, as they are for every other layout rule.
- **The one heading that fails it is separated.**
  The `Whole` heading in the review criteria gets its blank line.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 3 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: a heading can be swallowed by the list above it; the check reads the line as a heading regardless; nothing else measures the spacing. |
| Plan | Each of the 2 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py`: a heading needs a blank line above it; the one heading that fails it is separated. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC14, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

## References

- **R1.** [Shared skill guidelines](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9ed47b0d/skills/guidelines.md) — the Layout rules the check measures.

**Component:** skills/work-planner/references/work-breakdown.md

## Overview

The Work Breakdown Guide says a complete task's Coverage cell is empty, and nothing empties it. A row's Coverage states which of the epic's criteria that row delivers, which is a fact about the plan rather than a status, so a complete row names the same criteria an open one does. This task retires the sentence and gives the rule a check.

## Problem

- **The guide states a rule nothing holds.**
  The [Work Breakdown Guide](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/workspace/skills/work-planner/references/work-breakdown.md) says of an epic's Coverage column that a complete task's cell is empty. `skills/work-planner/scripts/sync.py` ticks Done and leaves the cell naming what the row delivered.
- **A run shows it.**
  A sync of an epic on this board, after its first task merged, ticked the two criteria that task covered, marked the row done, and left the row's Coverage cell naming both.
- **The sentence reads as a garbled neighbour.**
  Task grain says a delivered task's Coverage omits each criterion a further task adopts, so a row whose criteria a follow-up task delivers carries an empty cell. That is a rule about where a criterion is delivered, not about a row being finished.
- **Nothing reports a departure.**
  The format check does not read an epic row's Coverage cell against the criteria the row delivers, so a table can carry a wrong cell indefinitely.

## Proposal

- **Coverage names what the row delivers, whatever its Done cell says.**
  The guide drops the completion sentence, so one statement of the column stands and the table stays readable as a record of which row delivered which criterion after the epic closes.
- **The criteria a further task adopts still leave the cell.**
  Task grain is untouched: a row whose criteria have all been adopted elsewhere carries an empty cell, because it delivers none, not because it is finished.
- **The format check holds the rule.**
  It reports an epic row whose Coverage cell does not name the criteria that row delivers, so the column is measured rather than remembered.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 4 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: the guide states a rule nothing holds; a run shows it; the sentence reads as a garbled neighbour; nothing reports a departure. |
| Plan | Each of the 3 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/work-planner/references/work-breakdown.md`: coverage names what the row delivers, whatever its Done cell says; the criteria a further task adopts still leave the cell; the format check holds the rule. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/work-planner/references/work-breakdown.md`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC15, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

**Component:** skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py

## Overview

A unit of work is one task row, or the rows that name each other in Joins, and one unit is one pull request. The available-work report names one record folder for the unit, and Deliver Mode holds that a unit's record exists and its rows carry that record's link. The reserve operation derives a folder from each row separately, so a joined pair is held with two folders and its planning is split across them. This task makes the reserve operation hold a unit with the folder the report named for it.

## Problem

- **The folder is derived per row, not per unit.**
  [The reserve loop](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/fae97e9e/skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py#L325-L329) calls `names()` once for each task it is given, with that task's own id and Description, and writes the result as that row's link.
- **The function it calls is written for a unit.**
  [`names()`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/fae97e9e/skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py#L95-L100) documents its result as what one unit's **first** task id and Description give it, which is the folder the available-work report prints. Only the first row's call agrees with that report.
- **Two joined pairs were held wrongly.**
  Reserving a joined pair on an epic of this initiative produced one folder named for each row rather than one for the pair, and a second joined pair on the same epic was held the same way. Each pair is one pull request, so each needed one record.
- **Nothing reports the split.**
  No check reads a joined pair's two links against each other, so a unit whose work items sit in different records looks correct in the table.

## Proposal

- **One reserve call holds one unit.**
  The operation reads the Joins of the rows it is given and derives a single folder from the unit's first row, as the available-work report does, then writes that folder as the link of every row in the unit.
- **A row that joins nothing is unchanged.**
  Its unit is itself, so its folder is the one its own id and Description give it.
- **Release follows the same reading.**
  Each row of a released unit points to its own work-item file inside the one record, which is where the record's README already links them.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 4 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: the folder is derived per row, not per unit; the function it calls is written for a unit; two joined pairs were held wrongly; nothing reports the split. |
| Plan | Each of the 3 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py`: one reserve call holds one unit; a row that joins nothing is unchanged; release follows the same reading. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC16, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

**Component:** skills/gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md

## Overview

The gitnexus skill does not pass the shared skill-file check. One bold lead in its CLI skill file runs 119 characters against the limit of 100, so a run of the check over every skill in the repository ends non-zero on a skill no current epic touches.

## Problem

- **One bold lead exceeds the width the shared layout rule sets.**
  The shared guidelines put a bold label and its body on one line only when the two fit within 100 characters, indent included, and a longer body on the next line indented under the bullet. [`gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/fae97e9e/skills/gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md#L82) carries both on one line of 119.
- **It is the only finding gitnexus carries, and it keeps the run red.**
  The shared check reports nothing else against the skill, including under the two layout rules the check gained for command placement and mode sections. A run over all four skills cannot distinguish gitnexus being clean from gitnexus being unchecked while this stands.

## Proposal

- **The body moves to its own line under the bullet.**
  The label keeps its line and the sentence beneath it is indented under the bullet, which is what the shared guidelines state for a body too long to share the line.
- **The check settles it.**
  `skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py` reports no finding for the gitnexus skill afterwards.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 2 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: one bold lead exceeds the width the shared layout rule sets; it is the only finding gitnexus carries, and it keeps the run red. |
| Plan | Each of the 2 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md`: the body moves to its own line under the bullet; the check settles it. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC17, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

## References

- **R1.** [Shared skill guidelines](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/workspace/skills/guidelines.md) — the bold-lead width rule the file departs from.
- **R2.** [Shared skill-file check](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/workspace/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py) — the instrument that reports it.

**Component:** skills/workflow-canon/test/audit_fixtures.py

## Overview

The Workflow Canon skill's own test suite needs an engine checkout its fixtures never name a way to reach, so a session that does not already hold one cannot run 35 of its 71 tests. The suite should state where that engine comes from, or stand up its own, so a contributor can run the skill's tests from a fresh checkout.

## Problem

- **Half the suite fails on a missing environment variable.**
  [`AuditFixture.setUp`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9ed47b0d/skills/workflow-canon/test/audit_fixtures.py#L22-L25) fails the test outright when `CANON_TEST_ENGINE` is unset: `CANON_TEST_ENGINE must name an engine with its installed yaml package`. 35 of the suite's 71 tests fail that way in a session that has not set it.
- **Nothing states what the variable should name.**
  The message asks for "an engine with its installed yaml package". Neither the [skill's guidelines](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9ed47b0d/skills/workflow-canon/references/guidelines.md) nor its [SKILL.md](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9ed47b0d/skills/workflow-canon/SKILL.md) Dependencies say which checkout satisfies it or how to prepare one.
- **A failure reads as a regression.**
  The failures surface as 35 red tests rather than as skips, so a contributor running the suite after an unrelated change cannot tell an environment gap from a break they caused.

## Proposal

- **The suite states its prerequisite.**
  The skill's Dependencies name `CANON_TEST_ENGINE`, what it must point at, and how to prepare that checkout, so the prerequisite is readable before the suite is run.
- **An unmet prerequisite skips rather than fails.**
  `AuditFixture.setUp` raises `unittest.SkipTest` when the variable is unset, so an unprepared environment reports an unrun check rather than a defect.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 3 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: half the suite fails on a missing environment variable; nothing states what the variable should name; a failure reads as a regression. |
| Plan | Each of the 2 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/workflow-canon/test/audit_fixtures.py`: the suite states its prerequisite; an unmet prerequisite skips rather than fails. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/workflow-canon/test/audit_fixtures.py`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC18, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

## References

- **R1.** [Test record for the mode-file restructure](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-12-1319-i11-e12-w03-work-planner-mode-files/tests.md) — the run that observed the gap, under Evidence Gap.

**Component:** skills/gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md

## Overview

The shared skill guidelines state that a skill's `SKILL.md` holds no command of its own: a command the entry point names is specified in the file whose procedure runs it, or in the catalog. The GitNexus CLI skill states five command specifications in its entry point, so every reader of that skill loads all five to reach any one of them.

## Problem

- **Five specifications stand in the entry point.**
  [`gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/fb53546f/skills/gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md) carries `analyze`, `status`, `clean`, `wiki` and `list` under a Commands listing, which the shared skill-file check reports as `command specification in the entry point`.
- **A layout fault stands beside them.**
  The same file carries a 119-character inline bold lead against the 100-character limit.

## Proposal

- **The specifications move out of the entry point.**
  Into the file whose procedure runs each, or into a references catalog the skill's procedures link, so the entry point states purpose and routing and the reader loads one operation at a time.
- **The wide lead is wrapped.**
  Its body moves to the line beneath the bold statement, as the shared guidelines lay a bold lead out.

**Component:** skills/workflow-canon/references/coverage.md

## Overview

`skills/workflow-canon/references/coverage.md` states what coverage a kind of change requires in four parallel sections. Three of them say so in the third person and one says so as a command to the reader, and nothing in the file distinguishes the two. A reader following the imperative one runs the commands it names; a reader following its siblings selects observations. Settling the file on one voice makes the selection readable as a selection, which is the distinction the step rule leaves to the prose.

## Problem

- **One file states the same kind of thing in two moods.**
  [`## Main Coverage`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/d1dea57e/skills/workflow-canon/references/coverage.md#L80-L82) reads "Install Engine Dependencies, Run Engine Checks and Run Delivery Gate establish the baseline", and [`## Docker Coverage`](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/d1dea57e/skills/workflow-canon/references/coverage.md#L115-L117) reads "Check Shell Syntax for changed helpers and Validate Compose with disposable paths". Both select the coverage a kind of change requires.
- **The imperative section carries words that read as an order of work.**
  Its *then* and *after* state that one command depends on another, and an imperative sentence carrying *then* is what a route looks like. A reader cannot tell a dependency from an instruction here.
- **The step rule does not reach this.**
  A section calls the commands it names where its author wrote them as steps, so none of these four calls anything. The rule makes the file's silence correct and leaves the ambiguity in the prose it does not read.

## Proposal

- **The four coverage sections take one voice.**
  Each states what the commands establish for the kind of change it names, as `## Main Coverage` and `## Workspace Coverage` already do, so the file reads as a selection throughout.
- **A dependency between commands is stated as one.**
  Where an image must be built before a container can be exercised, the sentence says that, rather than leaving *then* to carry it.
- **A section that does direct the reader states numbered steps.**
  Should any of the four turn out to be a route, it becomes a procedure under the shared rule rather than keeping an imperative sentence.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Analysis | Each of the 3 frictions read against the evidence the References section names: one file states the same kind of thing in two moods; the imperative section carries words that read as an order of work; the step rule does not reach this. |
| Plan | Each of the 3 proposals reduced to the change it makes in `skills/workflow-canon/references/coverage.md`: the four coverage sections take one voice; a dependency between commands is stated as one; a section that does direct the reader states numbered steps. |
| Implementation | Those changes made in `skills/workflow-canon/references/coverage.md`, and in each file the Proposal or the references name. |
| Review | Each proposal traced to the friction it answers, and the files the change touches read for the behaviour beside it. |
| Test | AC21, each criterion as the epic states it, observed by the instrument that criterion ends by naming. |

## References

**Component:** skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py

## Overview

A section heading whose body the author emptied passes every check the skill files are measured by. The shared skill-file check reads headings for their anchors, their order and their nesting, and reads each command specification for its callers, but nothing asks whether a heading still has content under it. A restructure that carries the last item out of a section leaves the heading promising something the reader will not find.

## Problem

- **An emptied heading has already shipped.**
  The Work Planner command move left `## Sources` and `## Sessions` standing with no specification under them. A [link check](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/9a461bab/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py), 57 of its own tests and the skill's suite all passed over that state, and a reader found it.
- **The check reads around the gap.**
  Its heading pass measures duplicate anchors and level jumps, its specification pass measures callers, and its line pass measures bullets, leads and prose runs. A heading followed immediately by another heading satisfies all three.
- **A move is where it happens.**
  Every restructure under the skill-layout work carries items between files, and the count of items a section holds afterwards is not read by any instrument.

## Proposal

- **A heading with no content of its own is reported.**
  A heading followed by nothing but whitespace before the next heading of its level or above draws a finding, naming the heading and its file.
- **A heading that only introduces sub-sections stays clean.**
  A section whose body is its sub-headings is the normal shape of a reference file, so the rule reads the span to the next heading of equal or higher level rather than to the next heading of any level.
- **The rule binds every skill.**
  It stands in the shared check beside the placement and section rules, so it is measured over every skill in the repository rather than remembered by the author of the next move.

## Work Breakdown

| Part | Description |

## Overview

Nothing measures whether a section's text survived a move. A restructure that carries specifications between files is reviewed by checks that read placement, links, headings and behaviour, none of which read the carried body, so a specification damaged in transit reads as correct to every instrument. A comparison of section bodies between a branch and its base closes that gap and makes the review of a move mechanical.

## Problem

- **Damage has passed the full battery.**
  A restructure of the Workflow Canon skill corrupted four command specifications. A link check, 71 tests and a structural check all passed over the damage, and it was found by a person reading the files.
- **Each move since has carried the comparison by hand.**
  The Work Planner move and the Workflow Canon move each wrote a one-off comparison, ran it once and recorded its output in a planning record. The instrument is rewritten per move and kept nowhere.
- **A retarget is indistinguishable from an edit without normalisation.**
  A moved specification's links must change, because an anchor whose holding file changed must name the file that now holds it, so a raw diff of the two bodies reports every move as a difference and buries a real one.

## Proposal

- **A script compares the section bodies of two revisions.**
  Every third-level section in a given path is extracted at each revision, keyed by its heading, and its body compared. A section that changed file is still compared with itself, so a move reports as a move.
- **Link targets are reduced to their fragments.**
  A markdown link target keeps only its anchor for the comparison, so a retarget reads as a retarget and any other change reads as a difference.
- **The output is the review's evidence.**
  It names each section as identical, moved, added, removed or differing, prints a unified diff for each difference, and ends with the section count at each revision, so a section lost or emptied in the move is visible in the count alone.
- **It is run as a check.**
  It stands with the other skill scripts and is cited by the revise procedure that restructures a skill, so the next move runs it rather than writing it again.

## Overview

Sync Epic reports an epic base as draft when a merged task targets it and no open pull request merges it. Where an epic's review pull request has already merged mid-delivery, the base is level with its long-lived branch and no pull request can be opened on it, so the report names an action the reader cannot take.

## Problem

- **The condition reads the pull request, not the branch.**
  A merged task targeting the base and no open pull request merging it is enough to report a draft. Whether the base carries anything the long-lived branch lacks is never asked.

- **The action it names cannot be taken.**
  Opening a pull request with no commits between head and base is refused. A reader following the report learns that only by trying it.
- **A report nobody can act on trains the reader past it.**
  The draft line sits among lines that do require action, and an epic that merges mid-delivery is the ordinary case for a long epic.

## Proposal

- **The draft line asks what the base carries.**
  An epic base is reported as draft only where it holds a commit its long-lived branch does not. A base level with or behind its branch has nothing to review and draws no line.
- **The merged review pull request is not what the report turns on.**
  Whether a previous review pull request merged says nothing about what the base now carries; the comparison between the two branches says it directly.

**Component:** skills/work-planner/scripts/orphans.py

## Overview

Hoist mode offers every issue outside the agent-engineering structure as a candidate for placement. One class of issue is outside that structure because it is a test fixture: a target a write check changes so that no issue recording work is changed. It must stay open to be writable, and it belongs in no initiative.

## Problem

- **A fixture is offered as planned work.**
  [#924](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/924) exists so the GitHub library's write check has somewhere to write. List Orphans reports it among the hoist candidates, cited by the initiative whose check uses it.
- **Every placement the mode offers is wrong for it.**
  Keeping it as a task, epic or initiative makes a fixture into work. Subsuming it closes it, and a closed issue cannot be written to, which breaks the check it exists for.
- **Leaving it is the right answer and the mode cannot record that.**
  Leave is for an issue that is not initiative work, and the mode's Left rule then asks that it take a standalone issue's layout. A fixture has nothing to say in those sections, and it returns as a candidate on the next run regardless.
- **The label already states what it is.**
  `throwaway:two` marks the issue as a target rather than a record. Nothing reads it.

## Proposal

- **A labelled throwaway is no hoist candidate.**
  List Orphans reads the label and leaves such an issue out of both candidate groups, so the report offers only issues a placement could serve.
- **The label is what marks it.**
  An issue carrying a `throwaway:*` label is a fixture by declaration, which keeps the test in the data rather than in a list of issue numbers.
- **Hoist mode states the exemption.**
  The mode names the class it does not offer, so a reader meeting such an issue knows why it is absent rather than assuming the report missed it.
